Calaveras de Azucar (Sugar Skulls)

Served at: Dia de los Muertos

6-8 medium skullsPrep 45 min

Calaveras de Azucar, or Sugar Skulls, are iconic and vibrant decorations for Dia de los Muertos (Day of the Dead). These edible or decorative skulls represent departed loved ones and are placed on altars (ofrendas) as a sweet offering, symbolizing the cycle of life and death and celebrating the memory of those who have passed. Making them is a cherished family tradition.

Ingredients

  • 3 cups (600g) granulated sugar
  • 1 tablespoon meringue powder (for skulls)
  • 4-5 tablespoons water (for skulls)
  • 2 cups (240g) powdered sugar (confectioners' sugar)
  • 1 tablespoon meringue powder (for icing)
  • 3-4 tablespoons water (for icing)
  • Food coloring (gel or liquid, various colors)
  • Optional: Edible glitter, small candies, sequins for decoration

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the granulated sugar and 1 tablespoon of meringue powder. Mix thoroughly with a whisk or your hands to ensure even distribution.
  2. Gradually add 4 tablespoons of water to the sugar mixture, mixing with your hands until it has the consistency of damp sand. It should hold its shape when squeezed firmly. If too dry, add a tiny bit more water, one teaspoon at a time, until the desired consistency is reached.
  3. Firmly press the sugar mixture into clean, dry sugar skull molds, ensuring all crevices are filled. Overfill slightly, then level the back with a straight edge or knife.
  4. Carefully invert the mold onto a piece of cardboard or a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Gently tap the mold to release the sugar skull. If it crumbles, press it back into the mold and try again, ensuring it's packed very firmly.
  5. Allow the sugar skulls to air dry completely. Small skulls may take 8-12 hours, while larger ones can take 24 hours or more, depending on humidity. They should be hard to the touch before decorating.
  6. Once the skulls are completely dry, prepare the royal icing. In a medium bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar and 1 tablespoon of meringue powder.
  7. Gradually add 3 tablespoons of water, mixing until a thick, smooth icing forms. If it's too thick to pipe, add a tiny amount more water, half a teaspoon at a time, until it reaches a pipeable consistency (like thick toothpaste).
  8. Divide the royal icing into small bowls and tint with food coloring as desired. Use gel food coloring for vibrant colors without thinning the icing too much.
  9. Transfer the colored icing to piping bags fitted with small round tips (or use ziploc bags with a tiny corner snipped off).
  10. Decorate your sugar skulls with intricate patterns, dots, lines, and flowers. You can use edible glitter, sequins, or small candies to adorn them further while the icing is still wet.
  11. Allow the decorated skulls to dry completely for several hours (at least 2-4 hours) before handling or displaying to prevent smudging.

Tips

  • Ensure the sugar skulls are completely dry before decorating; otherwise, they may collapse or the icing may not adhere properly.
  • Work quickly with the royal icing, as it dries fast. Keep unused icing covered with a damp cloth or plastic wrap pressed directly onto the surface to prevent crusting.
  • Store finished sugar skulls in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. They can last for years as decorative pieces if kept dry.
